newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says S.E. Asia sought its help.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says S.E. Asia sought its help.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Thursday that several southeast Asian countries had asked Taiwan to support their currencies during that region's recent foreign exchange troubles.
Sheu gave no indication as to how Taiwan responded.

Despite a sharp depreciation in the Taiwan dollar in the past several days to its lowest level since 1988, Taiwan and its currency are seen clearly as not suffering from -- nor particularly vulnerable to -- the kind of speculative attacks that have shocked several southeast Asian currencies in July.
The bank has been seen by experts as tacitly welcoming, even encouraging, a well-tempered depreciation in the interest of stronger exports -- Taiwan's economic life-blood.
They say Taiwan's central bank, boasting imposing foreign exchange reserves of over US$90 billion, could easily defend the currency as it often has at times of political uncertainty.

The bank's strength was never clearer than during a long stretch in 1995-96 when it held Taiwan's dollar above T$27.5 despite military menacing by rival China that triggered a run on foreign exchange and gold and a flood of capital outflows.
Within two months after that crisis passed, the central bank said it was no longer defending T$27.5 -- setting the unit on a long, languid slide that dealers say has yet to play out.
